missionPremise.statement: OPS-21 S3 dispatch (_dispatches/2026-09-10_ops21-s3_dispatch.md, byte-identical to _catalog/dispatch_missions/mission_ops21_s3_non_vacuity.md): build a non-vacuity guard -- one test per registered write path asserting it CAN produce a real value on at least one realistic input, distinct from the existing dormant/starved reachability controls (check-live-job-has-config.mjs, writer-cli-reachability.test.mjs, both confirmed to live in hauska-factory).
missionPremise.authoritativeScopeCorrection: The dispatch's STANDING FACTS names computeTier1Envelope (legacy-design-tools) as the anchor instance with no repo-scope caveat, but doc_repo scripts/plan-progress.mjs --sql (the authoritative completion-predicate source per canon preamble 'a lane is done when its predicate says so') scopes S3's durable coverage to 'hauska-engine + hauska-factory' only, and the hard prohibition 'stay in your own repository... write only where your lane says' forbids committing to legacy-design-tools from this lane. Resolved by treating computeTier1Envelope as the anchor DEMONSTRATION of the technique (executed read-only in a throwaway, uncommitted, now-deleted worktree) and building the durable, committed guard only in the two authoritatively-scoped repos. Full reasoning in CP1.

scopeBasis.whyThisRepoBoundary: doc_repo's own plan-progress.mjs --sql names 'hauska-engine + hauska-factory' as S3's scope explicitly, distinct from L1/L2/L3 (legacy-design-tools' own, separately-owned predicates in the same predicate list) -- this is a deliberate exclusion the authoritative instrument already draws, not an oversight of this lane.
scopeBasis.whyWriteAllowlistAndScriptConventionAreT: Mirrors the program's own standing rule ('the closed set is derived, not hand-authored') applied one level down from rails to write paths: hauska-factory already had a code-owned registry (WRITER_JOBS) for exactly this purpose; hauska-engine did not, so the write-*.mjs naming convention (itself mechanically derivable by grep, not a hand list) was used instead, and is named as a gap this lane's registry work partially, not fully, closes -- hauska-engine has no allowlist as strong as hauska-factory's.
scopeBasis.whyF11AndEasementAreExcluded: See completionPredicate.hauska-factory.exclusionBasis above -- dormant, not vacuous, out of this guard's stated third-category scope.
scopeBasis.whyPurgeGateRemediateJobsWereIncluded: WRITER_JOBS makes no kind-based distinction for registration; all 21 implemented entries are 'registered write paths' by the allowlist's own definition, so all 21 received the non-vacuity framing, adapted per kind (a gate job's 'value' = reaching a real decisive verdict branch; a remediation job's 'value' = actually flagging a crafted collision, not always reporting clean; a purge job's 'value' = actually identifying a crafted orphan).

secondVacuousPathFound.target: hauska-factory src/jobs/p3-absence.mjs, function runP3Absence (writer allowlist id p3-rail-absence, planRow F-05/F-06)
secondVacuousPathFound.description: runP3Absence returns an identical {ok:true, applyExecuted:false, note:"dry classify/serve only; no store write"} shape for every county and every input, and never calls classifyParcelRail / classifyCountyEasement / writeRailAbsence / serveParcelBrief / serveParcelRail -- the real, independently-tested, genuinely capable absence-classification logic in src/ledgers/rail_absence*.mjs that both those modules' own header comments claim this job triggers. writer-cli-reachability.test.mjs does not and structurally cannot catch this: it verifies the job MODULE is imported by cli.mjs, not that the module's runtime function reaches the logic it documents. This is the third category the dispatch describes (built, tested in isolation, wired to a dispatcher, structurally incapable of a differentiated real value) found live in production code, not merely reasoned about via the motivating example.
secondVacuousPathFound.verifiedIndependently: Read src/jobs/p3-absence.mjs lines 1-64 directly (not just the sub-agent's report); confirmed by inspection that the function body is a fixed literal object with no branch on any input. Re-ran the two new tests myself: 15 pass / 0 fail / 2 todo, exit 0.
secondVacuousPathFound.status: Reported, not fixed, per explicit dispatch scope ('your job is the detector, not the repair'). Two tests exist at hauska-factory test/p3-absence.test.mjs (added in PR #133, merged), marked node:test `{ todo: '<reason>' }` so CI stays green while the finding remains live and re-triggerable. Re-enable path: remove the `todo` option once someone wires runP3Absence to the ledger functions -- at that point the tests become real, permanent regression coverage.
secondVacuousPathFound.disposition: Not this lane's to fix (out of scope). Flagged here for the planner/operator to route as its own card if desired.

constraintsHonored: Isolated worktrees only -- never touched P:/hauska-engine or P:/legacy-design-tools, both mid-edit by other lanes; the one scratch LDT worktree created for verification was read-only in effect (nothing committed) and deleted at close.
Stay in own repository -- no durable write proposed to legacy-design-tools; the anchor was demonstrated, not committed, there.
No write-slot taken -- no --apply run, no live Postgres/gcloud connection from any test.

MERGE only on CI check-run conclusion string 'success' -- verified via `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` (not `gh pr checks` prose) for both PRs before merging; SUCCESS confirmed on all 5 check-runs across both PRs before either merge.
Fan exactly one level deep -- 4 sub-agents, each prompt opened with the do-not-spawn clause as its literal first line, none spawned further (confirmed in each final report).
whatRemainsOpen: p3-rail-absence's actual repair (wiring runP3Absence to the ledger) is a new, separate finding for the planner to route -- not closed by this lane, deliberately.

hauska-engine has no writer-allowlist as strong as hauska-factory's WRITER_JOBS; the write-*.mjs naming convention this lane used is mechanically derivable but not a first-class, code-enforced registry the way hauska-factory's is. Worth a future card if the fleet wants CTRL-1-style one-source-of-truth parity between the two repos.

Whether legacy-design-tools' own L2/L3 lanes (already named in plan-progress.mjs's predicate list) plan a durable, committed non-vacuity test for computeTier1Envelope itself -- this lane's anchor treatment was demonstration-only by design; if no LDT lane is already carrying that, it is a real gap, surfaced here rather than assumed away.
